they complained to him, the Edessenes, about what they were suffering from those who lodged in their houses,
he replied:
"In the time of the Romans you were living in luxury in this land,
while our fathers were wandering in the desolate deserts pasturing camels in freezing cold and scorching heat.
And now that we have taken possession of this land by our sword,
why are you unwilling to surrender it to us?" And so the Edessenes departed without obtaining their wish.
And Tahir built a wall between Callinicus and al-Rafiqa,
and fortified himself.
And he gave himself over to reading, exposition, and study of the philosophers.
And in the year one thousand one hundred and thirty
(1130 of the Greeks,
819 of our Lord?), al-Ma'mun came from Khorasan to Baghdad,
and Ibrahim, his uncle, fled and hid himself,
and the Baghdadis submitted to al-Ma'mun.
And in the year 1132,
al-Ma'mun sent Tahir to Khorasan to rule over it,
and he promoted his son Abdallah and appointed him in his father's place.
Then Nasr the rebel took courage,
and bought the fortress of Beit Balash,
and gathered his army,
and encamped at Hani, a river near Callinicus.
And when Isa and the townspeople with him came out,
Nasr killed them all,
and plundered and took captive the villages.
Then al-Ma'mun sent against him Shabib, a mighty man of valour, with seven thousand picked Persians,
and they encountered Nasr, and the Arabs who were with him turned their backs.
And the Persians began plundering the poor townspeople,
eating and drinking and boasting as if they had defeated the rebel.
Then Nasr turned back upon them,
and the Persians were broken by panic.
And when Shabib saw that he was defeated,
he wished to go by night secretly toward Antioch.
Nasr, however, perceived it and pursued after him,
and cut off about three thousand of the Persians who were with him,
and captured them all.
And Shabib fled with a few men to Baghdad.
And Nasr came and hid in an ambush against the villages along the river Sajur,
Shughr which is beside Mabbug.
And when everyone went out to their work,
they fell upon them and killed men and women.
And when many of the peasants and poor folk went up to the monastery of Burim,
he set fire to it,
and some of them were burned.
And those who threw themselves down and fell and were broken,
he cut off their heads,
and carried them loaded with him to Sarug.
